content:
Twilio was added to the S&P 500 Equal Weighted Index and removed from two Russell small cap composite indices in early October 2026, reflecting a shift in how the business is classified across benchmark universes.

The index changes arrive alongside increasingly optimistic earnings estimates and broadly positive brokerage research, which together focus attention on Twilio's ability to convert higher-value customer engagement demand into sustained profitability.

We will look at how Twilio's investment narrative is influenced by this index reshuffle and the upgraded earnings outlook.

Scan how fund flows are rotating around Twilio's index move, then shortlist other potential beneficiaries using our curated list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (25 results) .

To be comfortable holding Twilio, you need to believe the customer engagement platform can keep turning rising usage of messaging, voice, email and data tools into durable cash generation. The near term hinge point is whether management can stabilise margins while revenue is forecast to grow at about 10.1% a year and net profit margins sit around 20.6%.

The biggest operational risk is that low margin messaging, carrier fees and regulatory costs eat into that profitability just as AI driven communications and omnichannel use cases are expanding. The recent index reshuffle itself does not fundamentally change those drivers, although it can influence who owns the stock and how volatile trading feels.

The most relevant recent development is Twilio's move into the S&P 500 Equal Weighted Index and removal from two Russell small cap composites. This shifts the ticker into portfolios that track larger, more diversified US companies and out of some small cap strategies that previously held it as part of their benchmarks.

Why that matters for you is how future catalysts translate into actual demand for the shares. If Twilio executes on AI powered communications, Segment cross sell and ongoing cost discipline, any change in fundamentals will now be reflected in a different mix of index and active funds. Risks such as earnings forecast declines or gross margin pressure could also feed through more quickly to that broader investor base.

Twilio Analyst Assumptions in Plain English

Twilio's narrative projects US$7.6b revenue and US$485.1 million earnings by 2029. That profile lines up with analysts baking in 10.8% yearly revenue growth and an earnings decline of about US$614.9 million from current earnings of roughly US$1.1b.

Learn how Twilio's fair value points to a 10% potential upside compared with its current price before the market closes the gap.

One alternative story around Twilio leans hard into regulatory and localization risk. The most cautious analysts were assuming only 9.3% annual revenue growth to about US$7.3b and earnings of roughly US$503.7 million by 2029, well below bullish estimates. The takeaway is straightforward: opinions were already wide before this index reshuffle, so views may continue to evolve as the impact becomes clearer.
